terra.problem: It assigns David a purpose for combining the images: so that the reader feels how serious the danger is. The psalm does not state that purpose.
It says David wants the whole record read, including the unflattering parts. That motive is not stated or marked as Papa Dorin's guess.
Saying David doesn't skip a single line suggests the list is a complete account. The psalm does not say that.
It states as fact that David is sure of himself. The psalm does not state his feeling.
It says David is showing how sure he is. That interprets his feeling and purpose without marking them as a guess.
The psalm mentions the fury of David's enemies, but does not say it is rising or give that as the reason for his request.

David's kingship is a fact from outside this passage without a supporting reference. The statement that a king stands in the same line as everybody else before the LORD also goes beyond what this passage says.
Saying God is not just checking what people do adds that He is checking their actions. This verse says He searches hearts and minds.
The cited verse, 1 Samuel 18:3, does not identify Jonathan as Saul's son. That detail needs its own supporting reference.
The explanation adds that the trouble does not stay small and grows. David's picture says the wicked man conceives trouble and births falsehood, without describing its size or growth.
The verse says the wicked man births falsehood, but does not say it becomes visible or known to others. Being born does not establish that it is no longer hidden.
It calls righteousness the same word used about God throughout the psalm. The earlier descriptions use righteous, not the exact same word.
